boards.title: Your First Weekend at George Washington University, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A practical under-21-safe first-weekend sequence linking Foggy Bottom campus anchors with nearby public parks, memorials, art, and performance spaces.

cards.title: Start at the Student Center
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Foggy Bottom campus orientation
cards.notes: Begin at the ground-floor hub, locate student services and dining, then note the H Street exit for the next campus stop.
cards.short_summary: Use GW’s main student hub to get oriented before exploring beyond campus.
cards.evidence_claim: GW identifies the University Student Center as the Foggy Bottom campus hub, with study, meeting, dining, and student-service spaces.
cards.source_title: University Student Center | Division for Student Affairs | The George Washington University
cards.access_notes: At the current summer schedule through August 16, 2026, the building is open daily 7 a.m.–9 p.m.; GWorld tap access begins at 6 p.m.

cards.title: Cross University Yard
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · A first walk through GW’s campus core
cards.notes: Enter from H Street, follow the brick paths through the lawn, and use the surrounding academic buildings to learn the campus layout.
cards.short_summary: A compact outdoor crossing introduces the physical center of Foggy Bottom campus.
cards.evidence_claim: GW places University Yard on H Street between 20th and 21st streets and describes its lawn, benches, trees, and converging brick walkways.
cards.source_title: GW Campus Venues | GW Events & Venues | The George Washington University
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus space; scheduled events or university operations may affect availability.

cards.entity_name: The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum
cards.title: Step Into the Textile Museum
cards.subtitle: Friday afternoon · Collections on GW’s own campus
cards.notes: Walk to 701 21st Street, check the current gallery list at entry, and choose one exhibition for an unhurried first look.
cards.short_summary: Shift from campus navigation to a focused gallery visit close to University Yard.
cards.evidence_claim: GW’s museum is located at 701 21st Street NW and opens its public galleries Tuesday through Saturday from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m.
cards.source_title: The George Washington University Museum and The Textile Museum
cards.access_notes: Public galleries are open Tuesday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m., and closed on university holidays.

cards.title: Find the Smith Center
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Learn where GW gathers for athletics
cards.notes: Walk to 600 22nd Street, photograph the entrance, and check the official schedule before deciding whether to attend an event.
cards.short_summary: Locate the campus arena now so a future game day feels straightforward.
cards.evidence_claim: GW Athletics identifies the Smith Center as home to basketball, volleyball, gymnastics, swimming and diving, and water polo competitions.
cards.source_title: The Charles E. Smith Center - George Washington University Athletics
cards.access_notes: Event access depends on the athletics schedule. The venue has a no-bag policy, with limited exceptions for screened medical and parenting bags.

cards.entity_name: The REACH at the Kennedy Center
cards.title: End Friday at the REACH
cards.subtitle: Friday evening · Riverfront architecture near Foggy Bottom
cards.notes: Follow the pedestrian approach to the Welcome Pavilion, explore the public grounds, and pause at the river-facing outdoor spaces.
cards.short_summary: Close the first day with an arts-campus walk beside the Potomac.
cards.evidence_claim: The Kennedy Center campus map identifies the REACH’s pavilions, plaza, gardens, lawn, pedestrian bridge, and riverfront spaces.
cards.access_notes: The published campus map lists REACH hours as 10 a.m.–midnight daily; performance spaces and individual events may have separate access rules.

cards.title: Begin Saturday at Lincoln’s Chamber
cards.subtitle: Saturday morning · A free National Mall landmark
cards.notes: Climb to the main chamber, read both wall inscriptions, then find the commemorative stone marking the 1963 speech location.
cards.short_summary: Start the Mall portion of the weekend with the memorial’s central civic texts.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service states that the Lincoln Memorial’s main chamber is free and contains Lincoln’s statue and inscriptions of two speeches.
cards.source_title: Visit the Lincoln Memorial Chamber - Lincoln Memorial (U.S. National Park Service)
cards.access_notes: The memorial is open 24 hours daily, but restrooms, museums, and elevators close in the evenings. The separate undercroft requires a timed ticket.

cards.title: Loop Through Constitution Gardens
cards.subtitle: Saturday late morning · A quieter route across the Mall
cards.notes: Take the winding paths around the lake and cross toward the island memorial, staying on established walkways and lawns.
cards.short_summary: Trade the Mall’s formal axis for a landscaped walk around water and trees.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service describes Constitution Gardens as a landscaped National Mall park with paths, lawns, a four-acre lake, and the 56 Signers Memorial.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor National Park Service site; paths and sections may be affected by maintenance, permitted events, or temporary closures.

cards.title: Explore Craft at the Renwick
cards.subtitle: Saturday afternoon · Free American craft near the White House
cards.notes: Enter at Pennsylvania Avenue and focus on one gallery floor; use the 17th Street ramp if step-free access is needed.
cards.short_summary: Add a manageable indoor art stop without leaving the Foggy Bottom area far behind.
cards.evidence_claim: The Smithsonian lists the Renwick Gallery as a contemporary American craft museum open daily from 10 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., free with no pass required.
cards.source_title: Renwick Gallery of the Smithsonian American Art Museum | Smithsonian Institution
cards.access_notes: Open daily 10 a.m.–5:30 p.m.; closed December 25. No pass is required, and the accessible entrance is at 17th Street.

cards.title: View the White House From Lafayette Park
cards.subtitle: Saturday late afternoon · Public space and presidential history
cards.notes: Walk the park’s perimeter, identify the surrounding historic buildings, and use the north side for a public White House view.
cards.short_summary: Connect a familiar national landmark to the history of its surrounding public square.
cards.evidence_claim: The National Park Service identifies Lafayette Park as a seven-acre park directly north of the White House with a long history of public gatherings.
cards.access_notes: The park is a public outdoor space, but the National Park Service warns that Secret Service closures may occur without advance notice.

cards.title: Close the Weekend With a Campus Reset
cards.subtitle: Sunday evening · Plan the week from a familiar hub
cards.notes: Return to the ground- or fourth-floor study areas, review Monday’s route, and check GW Engage for upcoming campus activities.
cards.short_summary: Finish where the sequence began, now with enough context to plan the first week.
cards.evidence_claim: GW states that study spaces of varying sizes are available on the ground and fourth floors of the University Student Center.
cards.source_title: University Student Center | Division for Student Affairs | The George Washington University
cards.access_notes: On August 13, 2026, summer hours are 7 a.m.–9 p.m. daily through August 16, with GWorld tap access required after 6 p.m.

warnings: The first and final cards use distinct named subjects within the same building: the University Student Center as an orientation hub and its officially identified study spaces as the closing activity.
Hours and temporary-access conditions should be rechecked immediately before visiting, particularly for the Student Center, Smith Center events, Lafayette Park, and Kennedy Center spaces.
